fieldData.guide-section-heading: How to find, vet and book conservative creators.
fieldData.guide-section-content:
Two kinds of conservative creator

“Conservative influencer” covers two groups that brands should treat differently.

  • Lifestyle and community creators. They post mostly about parenting, faith, homeschooling, the outdoors, home, fitness or food, and share their politics along the way. A product post from one of these creators works like any other brand partnership.
  • Commentators and news creators. Their content is mainly opinion on candidates, parties and issues. A paid post here can count as political content, which TikTok and Meta restrict (see below), and it needs a closer brand-safety review.

Decide which group your campaign is for before you search.

Find conservative creators on Jem Social

  1. Search a keyword. Start with topic words, such as “homeschool” or “hunting”. Add a word like “conservative” or “patriot” to narrow it.
  2. Narrow the list. Filter by platform, location, follower range and engagement rate.
  3. Read every profile. A keyword search finds profiles that match the word, not creators who fit your brand. Results can include organizations, campaign accounts and meme pages as well as individual creators.
  4. Message the creators you want in Jem Social, or post a brief and let creators apply to you.

Jem Social's niche pages group creators by topic, not by politics. They're another way in if your product fits one of them: mom, outdoor, lifestyle or fitness creators.

Vet every profile before you book

  • Read recent posts, not just the top ones. Scroll back a few months to see what the account normally posts.
  • Read the comments. They show who follows the account and how the creator talks to them.
  • Look at past brand deals. Check how the creator disclosed them and what the content looked like.
  • Check engagement for their size. Compare creators in the same follower range. The Engagement Rate Calculator works it out from any public profile.
  • Check the audience. Make sure where followers live and how old they are matches your buyers. Jem Social shows audience data on each profile.
  • Set the limits in writing. Say whether the sponsored post can mention politics, and get the creator to agree before they start.

Check the platform rules on political content

Paid posts about politics are treated differently from ordinary sponsored posts. This is what two platforms say, as of November 2026. Policies change, so read the current version before you brief.

PlatformWhat the policy saysRead it
TikTok
Doesn't allow paid political advertising across its monetization features, including creators being compensated for making branded political content.
Politics, governments and elections
Branded Content Policy
Meta (Instagram and Facebook)
Its Branded Content Policies list “controversial political or social issues or crises in an exploitative manner for commercial purposes” as prohibited content. Ads about social issues, elections or politics have a separate policy.
Branded Content Policies
Ads about social issues, elections or politics

YouTube and X have their own rules, which this page doesn't cover. A paid post about a candidate, party or political issue is a different case from a creator recommending a product, so keep the sponsored post to the product. This is a summary, not legal advice.

Put it in the brief

Write down what the creator needs so nobody has to guess:

  • The deliverables, deadline and budget. The Campaign Brief Generator gives you a template.
  • Talking points for the product, and whether the post can mention politics.
  • The disclosure. The FTC says creators must disclose any financial, employment, personal or family relationship with a brand, including free products. The disclosure has to be hard to miss, and in the video itself rather than only the description. Terms like “ad” and “sponsored” are clear. Its Endorsement Guides cover advertisers too. See the FTC's Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers.
  • Usage rights: whether you can reuse the content, including as paid ads.

What conservative influencers cost

Rates are set by each creator and depend on followers, platform, deliverables and usage rights, so there's no single price. The Influencer Rate Calculator gives a starting point. Put your budget in the brief, and agree on deliverables and usage rights before any content is made.

fieldData.faq-1-answer-3: Search Jem Social by keyword, then narrow by platform, location, followers and engagement rate. A keyword search finds profiles that match the word, so results can include organizations and campaign accounts. Open each profile and read recent posts before you shortlist a creator.
fieldData.faq-2-answer-3: It depends on the content. TikTok says it doesn't allow paid political advertising, including creators being compensated for making branded political content. A sponsored product post that isn't political is a different case. Read TikTok's Branded Content Policy before you brief.
fieldData.faq-3-answer-3: Meta's Branded Content Policies list controversial political or social issues or crises used in an exploitative manner for commercial purposes as prohibited content, and ads about social issues, elections or politics have a separate policy. Read both before you run paid partnerships or boost creator posts as ads.
fieldData.faq-4-answer-3: Yes. The FTC says creators must disclose a financial, employment, personal or family relationship with a brand, including free products. The disclosure should be hard to miss and in the video itself, not only the description. Terms like "ad" and "sponsored" are clear.
fieldData.faq-5-answer-2: A conservative creator can post mostly about parenting, faith, the outdoors, home, fitness or food. A commentator's content is mainly opinion on candidates, parties and issues. Platform rules on paid political content matter most for the second group, which also needs a closer brand-safety review.
fieldData.faq-6-answer-2: There's no single price. Each creator sets a rate based on followers, platform, deliverables and usage rights. Put your budget in the brief, and use the Influencer Rate Calculator for a starting point.
fieldData.faq-7-answer-2: Yes. On Jem Social you search creators, message them, agree on deliverables, and pay through Jem with funds held until you approve the content. It's $69/month, billed monthly, after a 7-day free trial, plus creator rates.
